The Artemis II mission successfully concluded on April 10, 2026, with a safe splashdown of the Orion capsule in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT). The four-person crew—Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen—returned after a 10-day lunar flyby, marking the first crewed deep-space mission in over 50 years. Key Highlights of the Artemis II Splashdown: Reentry: The capsule hit the upper atmosphere at approximately 24,000 miles per hour, generating temperatures around 3,000°F (1,649°C) before descending via parachutes. Recovery: The crew was retrieved by U.S. Navy divers and taken to the USS John P. Murtha for initial medical evaluations before returning to Houston. Mission Success: The mission confirmed the readiness of the Orion capsule and its life-support systems, paving the way for the future Artemis III lunar landing mission. Next Steps: Following the successful splashdown, NASA and its partners will analyze data from the trip to prepare for future moon missions.
